skill.name: altllm-portal-cli
skill.description: Coordinate AltLLM Portal CLI workflows across wallet authentication, API keys, billing, usage, crypto payments, and x402 credit top-ups.
skill.summary: Route multi-domain AltLLM Portal requests to the correct CLI workflow and focused skill.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives from Markdown code spans, fixed sibling documentation paths, and capability names. The skill routes agents toward API key changes, direct payments, and wallet signing without explicit user confirmation. This creates a medium business-logic risk.

remediation.issue: Sensitive account and payment actions lack an explicit confirmation boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Require user approval before API key mutations, wallet signing, payment execution, settlement, or any action that transfers funds.

content.value_statement: AltLLM Portal tasks span authentication, API keys, billing, payments, and x402 top-ups. This skill routes each request correctly and keeps Portal and gateway operations distinct.
actual_capabilities: Routes multi-domain Portal requests to focused authentication, API key, billing, payment, or x402 skills.
Distinguishes Portal account management from OpenAI-compatible gateway inference.
Maps wallet login, session status, and logout tasks to the authentication workflow.
Covers API key creation, inspection, updates, revocation, and model allowlists.
Coordinates balance, promotion, transaction, usage, crypto payment, and x402 top-up workflows.
limitations: This umbrella skill provides routing guidance, not complete command syntax for every workflow.
It relies on sibling shared setup documents and focused domain skills.
The current altllm CLI has no x402 command.
Plan access, model allowlists, payment support, and settlement depend on backend responses.

use_cases.title: Set Up Portal Access
use_cases.description: Log in with a wallet, inspect the session, create an API key, and verify the correct gateway workflow.

use_cases.title: Investigate Usage and Billing
use_cases.description: Review credit, transactions, usage summaries, timelines, models, and keys through the correct Portal commands.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Credit Top-Ups
use_cases.description: Choose a crypto payment or x402 workflow, check status, and verify the updated Portal balance.

prompt_templates.title: Check My Portal Account
prompt_templates.prompt: Use AltLLM Portal CLI guidance to check my wallet session, subscription tier, and current credit balance. Do not change account data.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Restricted API Key
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through creating an AltLLM Portal API key with a limited model allowlist. Ask for confirmation before creating the key.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Billing and Usage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Portal transactions and usage by timeline, model, and API key. Summarize unusual changes without exposing secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate a Verified Top-Up
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Portal credit top-up using the appropriate crypto or x402 workflow. Require confirmation before signing or paying, then verify settlement and balance.

output_examples.input: Check whether my Portal session is active and show my balance.
output_examples.output: The workflow checks session status first, then retrieves credit and plan metadata. It reports the result without changing account settings.

output_examples.input: Create a key for selected models and review recent usage.
output_examples.output: The workflow confirms the model allowlist, requests approval before key creation, then summarizes usage by model and key.

output_examples.input: Top up credit through x402 and verify the result.
output_examples.output: The workflow prepares a quote, pauses before wallet signing, tracks settlement, and confirms the updated credit balance.

best_practices: Use a focused domain skill when the request concerns only one Portal area.
Complete the shared preflight and confirm the active session and target before running Portal commands.
Require explicit approval before changing keys, signing wallet requests, or sending payments.
anti_patterns: Do not treat Portal account commands as OpenAI-compatible gateway inference commands.
Do not use the umbrella workflow when a single focused skill fully covers the request.
Do not assume Flex model access, payment support, or settlement success without checking backend results.

faq.question: What does this skill manage?
faq.answer: It coordinates AltLLM Portal authentication, API keys, billing, usage, payments, and x402 credit top-ups.

faq.question: Does it send model inference requests?
faq.answer: No. It manages the Portal side and distinguishes it from the OpenAI-compatible inference gateway.

faq.question: When should I use a focused skill?
faq.answer: Use a focused skill when the request stays within authentication, API keys, billing, payments, or x402.

faq.question: Can it manage Flex model allowlists?
faq.answer: It can guide allowlist workflows, but backend access checks determine which Flex model identifiers are permitted.

faq.question: Does the CLI support x402 directly?
faq.answer: No. The current altllm CLI has no x402 command, so the skill provides Portal x402 guidance.

faq.question: Should payment actions run automatically?
faq.answer: No. Wallet signing, payment execution, and settlement should require explicit user confirmation.
